chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Hāshim, from Sālim ibn Abī Khadījah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man asked him while I was listening, and he said: “I perform the fajr prayer, then I remember Allah, the Exalted, with whatever I wish to remember of what is obligatory upon me. I want to lie on my side and sleep before sunrise, but I dislike that.” He عليه السلام said: “And why?” He said: “I dislike that the sun should rise from other than its place of rising.” He عليه السلام said: “There is no obscurity in that. Look to where the dawn rises, and from there the sun rises. There is no hardship upon you in sleeping if you have remembered Allah.”
So the interpretation of these two narrations is that they indicate a kind of concession, even though what we have presented in the earlier narrations is more virtuous.

key_terms.أَذْكُرُ اللَّهَ: I remember Allah; engaging in dhikr after prayer
key_terms.الْأَفْضَلُ: that which is more virtuous or preferable
key_terms.الْفَجْرَ: the dawn prayer time, referring here to salat al-fajr
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: hardship or blame; indicating permissibility without distress or sin
key_terms.خَفَاءٌ: obscurity or ambiguity; meaning there is no uncertainty in the matter
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: the rising of the sun; the period before sunrise in question

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sleep after salat al-fajr and before sunrise if one has done dhikr?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on sleeping after salat al-fajr and after engaging in dhikr. It indicates that there is no harm in sleeping before sunrise once one has remembered Allah, though earlier narrations establish that remaining awake is more virtuous, making this report a concession.
